explanation: SET NOCOUNT OFF leaves row-count messages enabled, increasing client and network overhead.
SET XACT_ABORT OFF allows run-time errors to leave transactions partially applied.
SELECT * on Sales.Orders couples callers to all current and future columns and prevents covering index optimization.
SELECT TOP (10) from Sales.Orders without an ORDER BY returns an arbitrary, non-deterministic set of rows.
DISTINCT on o.OrderID is redundant because OrderID is already the primary key of Sales.Orders.
WITH (NOLOCK) on Sales.Orders can read uncommitted, missing, or duplicated rows.
Applying YEAR(o.OrderDate) in the WHERE clause prevents an index seek on OrderDate.
Comparing int column o.CustomerID to nvarchar(20) variable @CustomerIdText forces implicit conversion.
OR-based optional filtering (@CustomerID IS NULL OR o.CustomerID = @CustomerID) hinders cardinality estimation and index seeking.
Leading wildcard in o.Comments LIKE N'%urgent%' prevents an index seek.
NOT IN against Sales.Invoices.CustomerID can return unexpected empty results if the subquery produces NULL.
Wrapping o.CustomerID in ISNULL(o.CustomerID, 0) makes the predicate non-sargable.
Performing arithmetic (o.OrderID + 0) in the predicate prevents direct index matching.
Inequality predicate o.CustomerID <> 1 typically forces broad index or table scans.
CROSS JOIN between Sales.Orders and Sales.Customers without a join predicate multiplies rows.
Comma-separated FROM clause for Sales.Orders and Sales.OrderLines obscures join predicates.
Correlated scalar subquery on Sales.OrderLines executes per outer Sales.Orders row.
Correlated EXISTS on Sales.OrderLines checks per outer row instead of using a set-based join.
The CASE expression on o.Comments is duplicated in both the SELECT list and ORDER BY clause.
ORDER BY 2 relies on select-list position, which is fragile if columns change.
OFFSET 0 ROWS FETCH NEXT 10 ROWS ONLY orders by o.OrderDate without a unique tie-breaker.
UNION performs unnecessary duplicate removal between disjoint branches (OrderID = 1 and OrderID = 2).
Using COUNT(*) > 0 on Sales.OrderLines counts all matching rows when only existence is needed.
SELECT @OrderID = o.OrderID from Sales.Orders silently keeps the last value if multiple rows match.
Table variable @OrderIds can receive poor cardinality estimates.
SELECT ... INTO #ImplicitOrders creates the temp-table schema implicitly.
Cursor order_cursor processes Sales.Orders row by row instead of using a set-based operation.
WHILE loop processes iterations one at a time instead of set-based logic.
Concatenating @CustomerID into @Sql builds dynamic SQL without parameterization.
EXEC sys.sp_executesql @Sql executes dynamic SQL without parameterized inputs.
Temporary table #Scratch is created explicitly and not dropped before the procedure ends.
CATCH block selects ERROR_MESSAGE() without rethrowing or returning an error status.
Uses legacy RAISERROR instead of THROW.
Uses PRINT for diagnostics.
Hard-coded business identifier o.CustomerID = 1 embedded in query.
Unlabelled date literal '20160101' embedded in predicate on o.OrderDate.
CONVERT(date, '01/02/2016') omits an explicit style parameter, making it session-dependent.
COALESCE in the join predicate between Sales.Orders and Sales.Invoices inhibits join optimization.
Self-joining Sales.Orders on OrderID retrieves information already available in the single row.
ORDER BY o.Comments sorts by a wide nvarchar(MAX) column.
SUM(ol.Quantity) aggregates the entire Sales.OrderLines table without a WHERE filter.
HAVING ol.OrderID > 0 filters rows after grouping instead of in WHERE.
ORDER BY OrderCount is redundant on a single-row aggregate query without GROUP BY.
MERGE on Sales.Orders has documented concurrency and correctness edge cases.
UPDATE Sales.Orders SET Comments = Comments performs a no-op write that still incurs logging and locking.
DELETE FROM Sales.OrderLines WHERE Quantity = -1 uses a broad non-key predicate.
WAITFOR DELAY blocks the worker thread.
BEGIN TRANSACTION is not wrapped in a TRY...CATCH block.
SET IDENTITY_INSERT Sales.Orders ON alters session state and introduces fragile identity coupling.
EXEC sp_who invokes a stored procedure without a schema qualifier.
SET ROWCOUNT 1 changes a session setting without restoring it.
INSERT INTO #DemoCategories omits an explicit column list.
INSERT INTO #DemoCustomers omits an explicit column list.
Leading wildcard in CustomerName LIKE '%' + @CustomerName + '%' prevents an index seek.
User parameter @CustomerName is concatenated directly into dynamic SQL string @sql.
EXEC sp_executesql @sql executes dynamic SQL without parameterized inputs.
UPDATE #DemoCustomers lacks a WHERE clause and updates all rows.
Filtering o.OrderDate >= '2016-01-01' in WHERE converts the LEFT JOIN on Sales.Orders into an inner join.
DeliveryMethodID = NULL always evaluates to UNKNOWN instead of using IS NULL.
Scalar UDF dbo.GetCustomerType(CustomerID) in SELECT forces row-by-row evaluation.
CATCH block inside a transaction does not roll back the open transaction.
Hardcoded index hint WITH (INDEX = 1) on Sales.Customers restricts optimizer plan choice.
Query nests subqueries 4 levels deep; refactor using CTEs or temp tables.
Leading wildcard in CustomerName LIKE '%A%' prevents an index seek.
Calls multi-statement TVF dbo.GetCustomerOrdersMulti(@CustomerName) which has poor cardinality estimates.
